newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tennis-Hingis to face Capriati in battle of the prodigies.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tennis-Hingis to face Capriati in battle of the prodigies.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis and American Jennifer Capriati on Friday reached the final of the last warm-up event before the Australian Open to set up a battle between tennis prodigies past and present.
Hingis, widely regarded as the chief threat to world number one Steffi Graf in the Melbourne Grand Slam, defeated unseeded American Mary Joe Fernandez 6-3 6-2 in the Sydney International.
Capriati, the last player before Hingis to storm up the women's rankings in her mid-teens, proved too strong for compatriot Lindsay Davenport, winning 2-6 6-4 6-2 at White City.
In the men's singles, world number three Goran Ivanisevic was upset by Britain's Tim Henman in their semifinal to dent his preparations for the Open.
Capriati, who won this tournament in 1993 at the age of 16 before quitting the tour, is looking for her first tournament success since returning to full-time tennis.
"It's like I'm just starting my career now as a different person, just because I'm older," Capriati said. "It's just great being in the finals and playing well."
Henman defeated the Croatian top seed 4-6 7-6 (7-1) 6-1 in a men's singles semifinal to reach his second successive ATP Tour final.
Henman, who lost to American Jim Courier in Qatar on Sunday in his first ATP Tour final appearance, will face fellow non-seed Carlos Moya of Spain for the Sydney title on Saturday.
Ivanisevic fell away badly in the third set, prompting speculation about his motivation with the start of the Australian Open only three days away.
"I'm aware it was pretty clear that Goran was getting frustrated," said Henman. "But at the end of the day you've got to concentrate on what you're doing."
Moya, who will play defending champion Boris Becker in the first round at the Open, warmed up with a convincing 3-6 6-3 7-6 (8-6) win over compatriot and third seed Albert Costa in their semifinal.
